theorem.label: Theorem Th2 (V8).
theorem.text: A symmetric operator on ℂ^N is essentially self-adjoint: defect indices (0, 0); e^{−iHt} is unitary; Im⟨ψ, Hψ⟩ = 0.
theorem.proof: On ℂ^N every bounded symmetric operator is self-adjoint: D(H) = ℂ^N and the defect spaces ker(H* − iI), ker(H* + iI) are empty, since ‖(H ∓ iI)ψ‖² = ‖Hψ‖² + ‖ψ‖² ≥ ‖ψ‖² > 0 (the cross-term vanishes by symmetry). Consequences: real spectrum, e^{−iHt} a unitary group, ⟨ψ, Hψ⟩ real. Numerically: the minimal singular value of H − iI is 3.9 (theory: √(1 + min‖Hψ‖²) ≥ 1), the unitarity drift of e^{−iHt} is 2.2e-16 over 1000 steps. The limit part (L → ∞, essential self-adjointness of an unbounded operator) is the open obligation O03.

paras: Certificate: test_th2_selfadjoint.py checks three equivalent manifestations of self-adjointness — empty defects, unitary dynamics, real form — on the protocol gate; all three hold at machine floors. Practical value: the unitarity of e^{−iHt} underpins the dynamics campaigns (V17): the energy conservation 1.8e-15 in V17 is a direct corollary of Th2. The gap "finite-dim proved / limit open" is recorded honestly: in the infinite-dimensional problem symmetry is not enough, boundary conditions are needed (open boundaries are natural, but the strict convergence of resonances is an open problem of the program).
Boundaries: the theorem is finite-dimensional; the transfer to L → ∞ requires estimates of the essential spectrum and resonance geometry — see O03 in the obligation DAG.
